# Evidence
- Problem class: logsey-default-corpus-dir-is-live-install
- Model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
- Solved: 2026-10-02T05:16:07.671Z
- Verification: solution produced by pi in sandbox; see signatures.json

signatures.description: Running a locally-built logsey binary (go build -o /tmp/logsey-058 ./cmd/logsey) without --corpus-dir or $LOGSEY_CORPUS_DIR operates on ~/.local/share/logsey — the LIVE host install (58 registered sources, a ~96k-line corpus fed by a tailer). Reproducing a defect with a hand-written fixture by writing corpus.jsonl into the default dir clobbers the live corpus. Mitigations observed live: (1) the running tailer/QA re-appended the corpus from per-source checkpoints (offsets in checkpoints.json), restoring most content within minutes; (2) cleanup = remove only the fixture lines (match on the fixture's unique ts_ingested stamp + message substring), then `logsey index rebuild` to restore the index fingerprint. Always pass --corpus-dir <tmpdir> (or LOGSEY_CORPUS_DIR) for repro work; the repo's own tests use NewCorpusDirs(t.TempDir()) and never touch the default. Fix shipped for the actual defect LOGSEY-058: bare HH:MM ts bounds are rewritten to wall-clock CAST(date_trunc('minute', ts) AS TIME) comparisons before DuckDB sees them (internal/cli/index_query_tsbounds.go), matching mini_sql.tsAfter semantics; malformed bounds get a named error; verified live on the real 96k-row corpus (BETWEEN '18:40' AND '19:00' -> 6842 rows rc=0, was raw cast error exit 4).
